meta.title: TrACSS Good Practices
meta.source: TrACSS (Tracking AMR Country Self-assessment Survey) is run jointly by FAO, UNEP, WHO and WOAH (the Quadripartite) and tracks progress on multisectoral national action plans on antimicrobial resistance each year. National authorities and technical focal points fill it in online. WHO hosts the system. The 2025 round (the ninth) opened on 15 April 2025 in all six UN languages, after a record 186 countries (96%) responded in 2024.

meta.scaleNote: Progress levels A to E as shown in a country trend report; some questions are Yes or No. The scale and wording can change between rounds.
meta.note: The question list comes from one country trend report (Kazakhstan 2024), which shows selected indicators only; Section 1 questions were not seen and some questions in other sections may be missing. Wording is paraphrased. Check the official questionnaire for the round you work with. The crosswalk to JEE, SPAR and PHEPA is our own and is not official.

topics.title: How TrACSS relates to JEE, SPAR and PVS
topics.what: TrACSS is a yearly country self-assessment by the four Quadripartite organisations. JEE, SPAR and PVS are different instruments: JEE is an external evaluation, SPAR a yearly self-assessment of IHR capacities, PVS an external evaluation of veterinary services. A country can use the AMR parts of each to cross-check the others.
items: Overlap
JEE P4 (AMR), SPAR capacity C12 and PVS critical competency II-9 (AMR and antimicrobial use) cover the same ground as TrACSS sections 2 to 4.
Difference
TrACSS scores are self-reported by country focal points. They are not an external check.
